euler.proposition-8.1.markdown: **Proposition 8.1.** The data $U_j(0)$ converge in every $C^{m,1/2}$ to an odd divergence-free field $u_0$. In particular, $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3)$. Let $u$ be the maximal smooth solution of the Euler equations from $u_0$, with maximal time $T_*>0$, supplied by Section 1. Then $T_*\ge T_\infty$ and, for every $T<T_\infty$ and integer $m\ge0$, $U_j\to u$ in $C([0,T];C^{m,1/2})$. The solution is smooth and odd on $[0,T_\infty)\times\mathbb T^3$.

lean.fidelity_note: The formal statement retains bounded velocity and central vorticity tending to infinity. It additionally gives fixed constants $c>0$ and $C$ such that, on every sufficiently late interval $[t_j,t_{j+1})$, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$. This is a quantitative conclusion for the limiting solution, obtained from (8.2) by controlling the older-gradient term and later increments. The formal proof of Corollary 8.3 uses this extra bound; pointwise blow-up alone would not imply divergence of the time integral.

euler.proposition-8.2.markdown: **Proposition 8.2.** The solution has bounded velocity on $[0,T_\infty)$, and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\longrightarrow\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$.

lean.fidelity_note: The formal statement includes both limits in the paper: velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m(K)$ for every compact $K\subset\mathbb T^3\setminus\{0\}$ and every finite spatial order. Convergence is expressed for spatial derivatives of local extensions on neighborhoods of $K$, so it includes derivatives as well as values. Joint smooth extension through the terminal time is the separate conclusion of the auxiliary note.

lean.fidelity_note: The paper fixes the zero-mean Poisson pressure and normalizes $\max_{[t_0,T]}|\mathbf a(t,0)|=\lambda^{-3/4}$. The formal statement allows any smooth periodic parent pressure satisfying the stated residual and coercivity conditions, and requires only $0<|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le\lambda^{-3/4}$. Within this broader class, all powers in (5.34)–(5.38) agree, including the leading-level clauses, means beginning at level two, the correction $C_{p+1}$, and the remainder without an extra factor $\mathsf D^C$. The formal statement treats each finite depth $P$ and all retained levels, using constants $C_{n,p}$ independent of $P$; the constants for sums and the remainder may depend on $P$. Proposition 5.4 supplies every depth, and uniqueness makes their common levels agree. After fixing the envelope exponent, one parent exponent $C$ is chosen before the parent and is independent of derivative order, level, and depth. That same $C$ occurs in the hypothesis $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, and the same expansion satisfies every derivative order.
